title: Government to give bicycles to 300,000 schoolgirls to curb dropout
excerpt: Girls placed first, second or third in classes six to ten at 20,000 schools will get a bicycle. The Prime Minister test-rode samples on Wednesday.

image.alt: Two students cycle to school at sunrise in a village in Meherpur
image.credit: File photo: Ashikul Islam Anik / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
The government will give bicycles to 300,000 girls in classes six to ten at 20,000 schools across the country, to encourage them to stay in school, the state news agency BSS reported on Wednesday (25 November). Prime Minister Tarique Rahman rode several sample bicycles outside his office at the Secretariat that morning to check their quality, his deputy press secretary Md Suzauddowla said.

Under the initiative, the girls who come first, second and third in each class will each receive a bicycle, according to BSS. The education ministry organised the display of samples. The initiative aims to encourage girls in their studies and prevent dropout, BSS reported.

State Minister for Public Administration Abdul Bari, the Prime Minister's principal secretary ABM Abdus Sattar, Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani and the education ministry's senior secretary Abdul Khaleque were present. BSS did not report the cost of the scheme, the distribution date or how schools will be chosen.

Devlens could not find a published policy document or budget for the scheme.

Why it matters

A bicycle can make the journey to secondary school shorter and safer. But this scheme rewards the top three students in each class, who are the least likely to drop out. Education NGOs may want to ask whether girls most at risk of leaving school, including those facing early marriage, will benefit.

What to watch

  • The cost, funding source and distribution timetable.
  • How the 20,000 schools are selected, and whether madrasas are included.
  • Whether the scheme is extended to girls by need rather than class position.
